name: University of Michigan, Ann Arbor
summary: Major public research university campus in Ann Arbor, Michigan, with central, north, and medical campuses served primarily by on-site combined heat and power.

power.how_it_is_fed: Central Power Plant (CPP) at 1120 Huron St provides combined heat and power (steam and electricity) to most central and medical campus buildings via underground tunnels. North Campus primarily procured from DTE, with some CPP feed; ring bus design for redundancy.

buildings.name: Central Power Plant
buildings.why: Primary on-campus combined heat and power facility serving central and medical campuses.

buildings.name: Forest Avenue Switching Station
buildings.why: Electrical substation operated by University of Michigan, about 376 m from the centre of campus. From OpenStreetMap.

buildings.name: Ingalls Substation
buildings.why: Electrical substation operated by DTE Energy, about 499 m from the centre of campus. From OpenStreetMap.

buildings.name: University Hospitals
buildings.why: Main inpatient hospital complex with emergency department on the medical campus, approximately 1 mile from central campus core.

buildings.name: Bursley Hall
buildings.why: One of the largest residence halls by capacity on North Campus.

buildings.name: Mosher-Jordan Hall
buildings.why: Large residence hall in the Hill neighborhood serving many students.

buildings.name: Stockwell Hall
buildings.why: Major residence hall in central campus area with high resident count.

buildings.name: Alice Lloyd Hall
buildings.why: Large undergraduate residence hall near central campus.

buildings.name: Harlan Hatcher Graduate Library
buildings.why: Main research and study library serving the entire campus.

buildings.name: Michigan Union
buildings.why: Primary student union and gathering space with dining and events.

buildings.name: Angell Hall
buildings.why: Large classroom and academic building housing LSA departments and lecture halls.

buildings.name: Modern Languages Building
buildings.why: Major classroom and language instruction building on central campus.

buildings.name: Taubman Biomedical Science Research Building
buildings.why: Key biomedical research facility on medical campus.

buildings.name: Biological Sciences Building
buildings.why: Large research and lab building supporting multiple sciences.

buildings.name: Campus Safety Services Building
buildings.why: Headquarters for university police and public safety operations.

buildings.name: 1100 North University Building
buildings.why: Central Campus Transit Center serving as main bus hub.

buildings.name: William L. Clements Library
buildings.why: Special collections library and research resource.

buildings.name: Mary Markley Hall
buildings.why: Large residence hall in the Hill area with substantial capacity.

buildings.name: Undergraduate Science Building
buildings.why: Major classroom and lab facility for undergraduate sciences.

buildings.name: Rogel Cancer Center
buildings.why: Specialized inpatient and treatment facility adjacent to main hospitals.

transit.name: Blue Bus Central Campus routes
transit.connects: Central Power Plant, Michigan Union, Hatcher Library, 1100 North University Building, Angell Hall

transit.name: Blue Bus Medical Campus routes
transit.connects: University Hospitals, Rogel Cancer Center, Taubman Biomedical Science Research Building

transit.name: TheRide routes to North Campus
transit.connects: Bursley Hall and other North Campus housing to central campus transit hub

placement.note: Positions come from OpenStreetMap. Which building is on which feed is assumed: each is put on its nearest power source.
